## Additional Features - **Building Collision** — A buildings index is included for all non-filtered buildings, assigning each a flat foundation depth of **−10 m** in-game. This provides underground collision geometry so that tunnels interact correctly with building footprints. - **Water Depth Index** — A water depth index restricts track placement in water bodies. Coastal bundles include a real bathymetric layer derived from EMODnet Bathymetry (1/16 arc-min DTM, ~115 m resolution); inland water (rivers, lakes, canals) uses a flat **−4 m** index that prevents surface-level track placement. - **Ocean Foundations** — A depth-colored ocean floor layer is included for coastal bundles, providing a visual representation of Baltic Sea bathymetry visible on the in-game map. - **Place Name Labels** — Two layers of place name labels are embedded in the map: - _City labels_ — Major Polish cities at the metropolitan scale (gminy miejskie within Functional Urban Areas). - _Municipality labels_ — Names of all gminy within the map boundary. ## Methodology This map is generated through a six-phase pipeline that transforms Polish government census and employment statistics into georeferenced origin/destination demand points. **Point Seeding:** Candidate points are placed within each _rejon statystyczny_ (sub-municipal census unit, BREC) using population-weighted centroids derived from a hybrid 125 m / 250 m / 1 km mesh — GUS NSP 2021 published gridded population at native resolution where available, and a GHS-POP 100 m raster (JRC R2023A) gated by a BDOT10k residential building mask in dense urban tiles. **Mesh Reconciliation:** Initial point populations are refined by solving a constrained convex optimization that approximates each point's mass to residential and economic mesh ideals while preserving NSP 2021 (_Narodowy Spis Powszechny 2021_) per-rejon population totals. **Aggregation:** A global scaling factor reconciles the mismatch between boundary-captured employed residents (from NSP 2021) and workplace employees (from GUS BDL workplace-employment statistics broken down by industry section), since commuters cross the FUA boundary in both directions. **Commute Assignment:** Commute flows are assigned using a gravity model with distance-decay. Per-gmina origin-destination targets are taken from the GUS NSP 2021 commuter matrix; an iterative calibration loop adjusts gmina-pair multipliers until simulated commute shares converge to the observed flows. Where available (Warsaw and Wrocław city commute behaviour surveys), a sub-gmina rejon × rejon overlay is layered on top of the gmina-level assignment. **Special Demand Injection:** Non-commuter demand generators — airports, universities, hospitals, military installations, tourism attractions, sports leagues, theatres, and convention centers — are injected as an additive layer. Airport demand from ULC (_Urząd Lotnictwa Cywilnego_) statistics; university demand from POL-on (_Zintegrowany System Informacji o Szkolnictwie Wyższym_) registry × GUS per-institution higher-education enrollment, scaled by the national full-time student fraction; attraction demand from POT (_Polska Organizacja Turystyczna_) annual-visitor reports across all 16 _województwa_ (~960 attractions). Sports league demand is per-club average attendance × home matches across Ekstraklasa football, PHL ice hockey, PlusLiga volleyball, and Superliga handball; cultural-venue and convention-center demand from operator annual reports and PIPT (_Polski Związek Organizatorów Targów_) aggregates. **Layout Reconciliation:** A final spatial pass resolves point overlaps and ensures map clickability while keeping special-demand locations fixed. ## Data Sources All demand modeling is derived from freely available Polish government statistical datasets and public geospatial resources. ### Census & Demographics - **Workplace Employment Statistics** (per-municipality workplace count broken down by industry section) — [GUS BDL / Bank Danych Lokalnych](https://bdl.stat.gov.pl/) - **Sub-gmina commute surveys** (per-rejon residence × workplace cross-tabulations from Warsaw and Wrocław city travel-behaviour surveys, where available) — [Warsaw](https://transport.um.warszawa.pl/) · [Wrocław](https://www.wroclaw.pl/) ### Geospatial Reference -
